Catheters impregnated with chlorhexidine and sulfadiazine silver on the external luminal surface, appear to be effective in reducing both catheter colonisation and related bloodstream infection in high-risk patients when used within 14 days.9 Central ve- nous catheters impregnated with minocycline and rif- ampicin have been reported to be associated with a lower infection rate than standard silicone catheters10 and those impregnated with chlorhexidine and sulfadiazine silver.11 Guidelines have been produced for the prevention of in- fection associated with both peripheral intravascular and central venous catheterisation.12-14 1.
